gap_records.summary: Required candidate file for `native_godot_project` is unverified.

task_specification.objective: Replace the bootstrap with a playable survival-foundation movement slice whose keyboard and gamepad controls drive a camera-relative CharacterBody3D motor, an explicit readable dash lifecycle, stable collision sliding, clean pause/resume, and a bounded high-angle arena camera without FPS/TPS drift.

diagnosis.root_cause: The candidate is only the generated PRD bootstrap: its main scene contains a bare Node, and it has no gameplay scene, InputMap actions, CharacterBody3D motor, dash state ownership, or high-angle Camera3D. The required check is formally unverified rather than failed, but the candidate implementation cannot yet exercise any part of its movement, dash, framing, or pause/resume contract.

stop_conditions: Do not expand this task into automatic combat, enemies, experience drafts, the complete HUD, waves, boss behavior, or run-result lifecycle work assigned to later gaps.
Stop and correct the scene boundary if the configured main scene does not boot directly into an inspectable movement arena without parser, resource-load, or runtime errors.
Do not accept a dash implementation in which normal movement, dash, pause, or another subsystem can write velocity or invulnerability concurrently.
Do not claim the gap complete from source inspection alone; host and Tester runtime evidence must exercise ordinary keyboard and gamepad-equivalent input.
If visible presentation is added or rebound, keep it style-coherent and runtime-inspected; do not promote untextured primitive or debug geometry as final Mournlight art.

strategy.rationale: Build the missing capability as one authoritative locomotion cluster: InputMap bindings feed a single player motor and dash phase owner, while a separate damped high-angle camera consumes player motion only for framing. This directly creates the smallest truthful player-facing slice needed for the selected contract and keeps unrelated survival systems out of scope.

code: Developer runs the focused Godot import/boot and parser check and confirms there are no missing resources, invalid InputMap actions, script errors, or runtime errors.

Inspect the movement cluster to confirm camera-plane projection, diagonal normalization, one authoritative velocity writer, explicit dash phases and timers, active-only invulnerability, collision-aware motion, and pause/reset cleanup.
Inspect project input bindings for WASD, Space, Escape, left-stick axes, gamepad south, and gamepad start, with deadzones that cannot create idle drift.
runtime: Host and Tester use ordinary WASD and gamepad-equivalent left-stick input in several camera-relative directions, including diagonals and movement into an obstacle, and verify planar displacement, normalized speed, responsive stopping, and stable sliding.

Host and Tester exercise idle-to-anticipation-to-active-to-recovery-to-cooldown dash sequences using both input families, including held-button and rapid-repeat attempts, while correlating visible behavior with dash phase, velocity, cooldown, and invulnerability state.

Host and Tester pause and resume during ordinary movement and during each meaningful dash phase, verifying frozen progression, retained high-angle framing, no stuck input, no cooldown bypass, and no unintended action on resume.
GameLoop Runtime reruns survival_foundation_camera_movement_dash_contract and records the formal pass verdict; recapture and gap closure remain host/Tester-owned.
visual: Capture the shipped gameplay camera at spawn, sustained locomotion near an obstacle, dash anticipation/onset, and recovery; each frame must keep the player, collision context, and a useful escape direction readable.

Compare matched locomotion and dash frames to verify bounded damping and movement lead without severe lag, edge-hidden threats, repeated occlusion, free orbit, shoulder framing, or first-person drift.

Verify that anticipation, active dash, and recovery are visually distinguishable at normal gameplay scale and that the presentation remains coherent with Mournlight's stylized moonlit high-angle direction without debug or untextured geometry being presented as final art.

done_when: The configured main scene boots into a bounded 3D movement arena containing one CharacterBody3D player, collidable boundaries or obstacles, and one active high-angle perspective Camera3D.

WASD and gamepad left-stick input produce normalized camera-relative planar movement with responsive acceleration and deceleration, stable wall sliding, and no vertical drift or diagonal speed advantage.
The physics body remains the sole movement authority while a separate visual-facing child is updated independently, so presentation rotation cannot redirect or destabilize collision motion.

Keyboard Space and the gamepad south button start one dash sequence with observable anticipation, active displacement, recovery, and cooldown; invulnerability is true only for the declared active window, and held or repeated input cannot bypass cooldown.

Dash displacement respects collision, cannot tunnel through the arena boundary, and returns to ordinary movement without stuck velocity; pausing during locomotion or any dash phase freezes progression and resumes without latched input or an unintended dash.

The camera remains damped, high-angle, non-orbiting, and arena-readable throughout ordinary movement and dash, retaining the player, nearby collision context, and useful space in the travel direction without entering first-person or shoulder framing.

Relevant controller state is inspectable through stable runtime properties or signals, including movement input, velocity, locomotion state, dash phase, dash cooldown remaining, and dash invulnerability, without exposing a release-facing debug overlay.

The project completes a focused boot and parser check without errors, and directly related source inspection shows one authoritative velocity writer, one dash-phase owner, and explicit pause/reset handling.
tasks.instructions: Replace the PRD bootstrap with a native Godot survival-foundation movement scene. Define keyboard and gamepad InputMap actions for movement, dash, and pause. Implement one CharacterBody3D-based controller that projects camera axes onto the arena plane, normalizes input, owns acceleration/deceleration and collision sliding, and rotates only a separate presentation root for visual facing. Model dash as explicit anticipation, active, recovery, and cooldown phases under the same controller; normal movement may resume as designed outside the active dash phase, but no second system may write velocity or invulnerability. Make active-window invulnerability and cooldown state inspectable, reject dash retriggering from held input, and handle pause/resume and scene reset without stale input or timers. Add a gently damped high-angle perspective camera with bounded movement lead and no orbit/FPS/TPS modes. Provide enough bounded collision and style-coherent, high-angle-readable presentation to judge movement and dash, while keeping any mechanics-only stand-ins explicitly non-promoted and avoiding unrelated content expansion.
tasks.title: Establish camera-relative movement, dash, and high-angle framing
